Grey coloured siliciclastic rocks alternating from pinched sandstone lense rich sections to lense poor sections. Sandstone lenses are hosted within darker grey coloured, laminated mudstone. Sandy lenses become deformed and ptygmatic around 57-61m depths. Weakly oxidized fractures until 61m depth. Veining is minor (2% total) and calcitic (Fg). Most veining is bedding parallel (35 degrees) with a lessor crosscutting vein set. Minor local sections of gouge and carbon rich faulting (bedding parallel- thrusting?). Lower contact is faulted.

Grey coloured siliciclastic rocks. Alternating laminations of lighter sandy silt and darker mudstone. Very local, weakly calcereous mudstone lenses. Veining ranges from mm-dcm cale (8% total) and silica-calcite (Fg).Veins show weakly extensional internal fabric. Most veining is bedding parallel (35 degrees) with a lessor crosscutting vein set. Minor local sections of gouge and carbon rich faulting (bedding parallel- thrusting?). Lower contact is sheared and faulted (bedding parallel - thrusting?).

Grey coloured siliciclastic rocks. Alternating bands of lighter sandy and darker mudstone (fining upwards). sandy layers are medium to coarse grained. Most veining is bedding parallel (50 degrees) with a lessor crosscutting vein set. Minor local sections of gouge and carbon rich faulting (bedding parallel- thrusting?). Lower contact is ??????

Minor spotty playgorskite(white)/hydrozincite along fractures.The lower contact is marked by a cb-rich fault leading into weak to moderately recrystallized limestone.

Light grey MLS, minor intervals of fossils (amphipora), weak to moderate patchy recrystallization with subordinate dissolution features. The lower contact is marked by increase in amphipora abundance. Minor irregular calcite veinlets (1-3%).

Grey MLS. The upper contact is represented by increase in amphipora abundance lighter grey in colour representing minor recrystallization. The lower contact is a gradational tranistion leading into a lime mud unit with decreased fossil content.
MLS, mudstone represented by increase contents of dark grey micritic mud with minor amphiroa.  The lower contact is marked by a high angleTCA  styolitic contact leading into stromatoporoid-rich unit.

Light grey fossiliferous MLS (2). The stromatoporoid-rich unit (rudstone) with amphoria. The stromatoporoids range in size from 0.2-5 cm with minor embayments along stromatoporoid boundaries (dissolution 1 feature). Minor graphitic stylolite�s are observed throughout interval.  The lower contact is marked by a gradational contact leading into an interval matrix supported interval with amphorphia.  Minor irregular calcite veinlets (1-3%).

MLS, Light grey wackestone. The fossils consist of amphiora (10-12%). The upper porition of the interval is moderate to strongly altered by secondary dolomite. The lower portion is altered by weak to moderate patchy recrystallization, with increase in calcite veining intensity (moderate; 15-20%). Galena (0.1%) stringer observed at 302.47 m.

Light grey crystalline MLS (85%) with minor locally darker coloured fossil beds (Wackestone; 15%) containing amphiora (5-10%). The light grey crystalline MLS intervals are weakly foliated with weak green-brown sericite alteration (pervasively) along fractures, possible shear plane (366.45 m)? and replacing the matrix of fossiliferous intervals (376.44-376.80 & 374.70-374.90 m; pseudo breccia?). Minor (1-2%) fine grained pyrite associated with the sericite alteration. Trace irregular calcite veinlets (1-2%). The lower contact is marked by a gradational transition into recrystallized MLS with no sericite alteration observed.

Dark grey MLS, The lower contact is marked by a weakly brecciatd marble/ possible calcite vein (413.47-413.90 m). At 413.90 a  sercite halo leading into a sharp high angle contact leading into yellow-brown intrusive.

Yellow-brown pervasively sercite altered intrusive with spotty light green phenocrysts ( chlorite alteration? fluorite or apatite?). Possibe circular dark grey amygdules (2-5%)? The lower contact is marked by sharp irregular alteration halo contact (high angle TCA?) leading into dark grey MLS.

Possible exhalte unit. upper contact is a rubbly orange oxidized to darker grey mudston. sulphide pitting. Exhalte is mix between dark grey mudstone with qtz viening and a buff colord part with strong oxidation of fracture surfaces. interspersed dism py. minor sericite presence.

calcareous mudstone. calcite veinlets present, becoming abundant towards lower contact. calcareous beds are strongly reactive to hcl. mix between dark grey mudstone beds and a lighter grey bed. dism py. lower contact is gradational, becoming more graphitic.

Graphitic mudstone, fine grained and fairly soft with shiny fracture surfaces. Unaltered. Widespread thinly sheeted calcite veinlets, possibly following bedding. Possible slickensides on fracture surfaces. Minor pyrite, often in blebs 1-2cm, sometimes hosted in veinlets. Also in fine grained bands (eg at 95.20m) and disseminated. Small fault infilled with gouge from 95.14-94.18m.

Dark grey mudstone rhythmically interbedded with lighter grey siltstone/fg sandstone. Unaltered, moderately graphitic but less so than previous interval. Beds typically less than 1cm thick, non-calcareous, dipping moderately (40-60 degrees) relative to core axis. Mudstone beds have well-developed foliation, expressing distinct intersection lineation on fracture surfaces. Local syn-sedimentary deformation, otherwise beds are generally planar. Severall sets of extensional calcite veinlets cross-cutting bedding. Several massive quartz veins (eg at 112m, 119m), milky white and up to 10cm thick. Widespread very fine grained disseminated pyrite, also occurring in stratiform bands up to 2cm thick (eg at 104.69m) and sometimes hosted in calcite veinlets. Sphalerite(?) (brownish-red, soft, reddisn streak) blebs in calcite vein at 132.75m. Aresenopyrite(?) (darkgrey/silvery, very hard, triangular habit) in quartz vein at 158.35m. Lower contact interbedded with sandier (coarser-grained) interval.

Dark grey medium-grained unaltered sandstone. Upper contact interbedded with mudstone and siltstone, lower contact faulted. No bedding visible. Fairly incompetent, several rubbly fault zones (eg 162-163.00, 167-168m, 171-173m). Rare calcite veinlets, no preferred orientation. Widespread pyrite from 169.20-170.30m, disseminated in fault rubble, along fracture surfaces, and blebby in veins. Otherwise rare, and no other mineralization observed.
Large fault zone near contact with McDame. Sandstone and mudstone rubble, separated by significant intervals of dark grey clay-ey gouge. Rare disseminated pyrite.

Dark grey graphitic mudstone. Thin parallel bedding, some rubbly zones (likely faults). Especially graphitic (soft, shiny) from 205-207m. Rare calcite veinlets parallel to bedding. Occasional stratiform bands of fine grained pyrite (eg 194.86-194.90m), rare individual grains up to 3mm. Gradational contact with underlying interval, increasing calcareous beds.

Dark grey mudstone with lighter grey calcareous interbeds typically .5-2cm thick. Gentle to moderate effervescence. Erratic calcite veinlets, sometimes concordant with bedding, often not, and typically discontinuous. Trace disseminated pyrite. Moderately carbonaceous. Abrupt contact with McDame limestone below.

Start of McDame limestone. Upper contact is sharp with rubbly earn mudstone. This interval is moderat grey to a light recrystalized grey. stong semi massive pyrite is present for the majority of this interval. patchy recrystalization is intermixed with a darker grey blue limesstone, with angular contacts. qtz and carbonate veining is common throughout. lower contact is a stylolitic and demonstrates change to a darker limestone with possible dolomitic alteration.

Zone contains multiple short breccia zones (10-20cm) angular MLS clasts with carbonate matrix. these short breccia zones are continous dolomitic altered limestone.Strong pyrite mineralization is present from about 225 to 226m. mineralization is semi massive (25%). lower contact is a sharp change to a dense amphipora bed.

First observed fossiliferous MLS beds within this hole. dense amphipora beds make up aproximatly 90% of this interval. MLS ranges from a light grey to a darker possible dolomitic altered in patches. the lighter grey is possibly recrystalized. fossils all appear to be recrystalized. lower contact is styolitic.

Stromatoporoids intermix with amphipora beds. appear recrystalized. some fuative calcite present within the interval. light grey with darker dolomitic alteration patches. localized hydrothermal brecciation alternates between intense calcite veinlets.

Fault breccia zone. Gouge present at 284.57, with prominent slicks. gouge is a calcareous mud, white to grey. MLS clasts hosted in calcite matrix. Breccia above and below the fault zone. coarse calcite crystals present in localized void space. trace to no mineralization.

Strong recrystalization to marble. subtle angular clasts are present from a relic breccia. py strings grow in abundance moving to the lower contact, until there is semi massive pyrite filling the final 10 cm of the interval. Mineralized YBR. Fine grained sand, coaser than MLS. Pyrite mineralization is common within the YBR along fracture planes (5-10%). clay and rubble is present along natural fracture planes. Lower contact is an abrupt fault.

The fault gouge displays light folliation. carbonate veinlets are present. lower contact grades darker to the graphitic shale, then the shales become compitent.

dark grey to black strongly graphitic shale or mudstone.  trace sand lenses or beds present. minor quartz and carbonate veining throughout. localized brecciation occurs around 330m, clasts are dark grey to black angular to sub angular earn fragement held in a muddy matrix. beginning of interval is rubbley, though moving down from fz (upper contact) earn starts to become more competent. at around 328m rubble is nearly absent. sparce pyrite blebs are common throughout the interval. Dark grey 'sandy' fossiliferous limestone (weak presence of bulbous stromatoporoids, and elongated amphipora). Upper contact is gradational. Patchy disseminated anhedral 'dirty py' (1-3%) throughout following stylolites, white calcite veinlets and along vein margins. Localized semi-massive (~15-20%) anhedral 'dirty py' from 364-366m. Trace localized galena (1%) stringer vein, and  disseminated to blebby red-purple sph (1-2%) within white calcite veinlets and vein margins. Localized patches of weak to moderate light grey, recrystallized limestone, preferantially recrystallizing stromatoporoid fossils. Moderate patchy dark grey 'sandy/black sugar' limestone, possible secondary dolomitization (weak effervescence)? Weak to moderate patches of white calcite veinlets, stringers, and infilling microfractures. Localized undifferentiated microfaulting (~379.60m, ~384.15m), strongly overprinted by calcite infilled microfractures, and trace sulphides (py, sph) within the matrix. Fault planes are moderately graphitic with weakly developed slickenlines, and slickensides. Lower contact is faulted, leading into a black calcareous collapse/dissolution 2 breccia.

Black laminated calcareous mudstone (90%) with subordinate subangular matrix supported clasts of light grey limestone (10%). Upper contact is faulted with finely milled, matrix supported subrounded to rounded clasts of black mudstone, and light grey limestone. Trace disseminated subhedral py (1-2%) within matrix, along stylolites, and laminations. Localized patchy monomictic hydrothermal breccia's throughout, consisting of, blocky angular clasts of black calcareous mudstone, suspended within a fine grained white calcite matrix. Localized palygorskite along fracture planes, with moderately preserved slickenlines (394m). Lower contact is faulted, leading into light grey limestone.

Grey to light grey fossiliferous limestone (bulbous stromatoporoid, and minor amphipora). Upper contact is faulted. Trace (1-2%) disseminated 'dirty py' along fractures, stylolites, and white qtz-carb veins, veinlets, and stringers. Moderate localized qtz-carb vein intensity (401m). Weakly recrystallized limestone near upper contact, transitioning into moderate to strong light grey recrystallized limestone downhole (semi-pervasive). As recrystallization becomes stronger, disseminated dirty py is mainly concentrated along fractured surfaces, and along crosscutting calcite stringer vein margins. Presence of strongly microfractured, matrix supported, undifferentiated fault breccia (407m-409.60m). FBRX clasts of finely milled, subrounded, light grey to dark grey limestone are suspended within a calcite matrix. Lower contact is diffuse, transitioning into a possible sericitized intrusive? or altered limestone?

Moderately vuggy, and weakly brecciated, biege/buff sericitized YBR intrusion? or altered limestone? Upper contact is diffuse. Subangular clasts of grey limestone (5%) are fine grained, and suspended within a sericitized matrix (95%). Lower contact is faulted, leading into light grey limestone (MLS). Possible amigydules (>1mm micro pits) throughout.

Light grey to buff/beige limestone. Upper contact is faulted. Trace 'dirty py' (1-2%) along stylolites, fractured surfaces, subrounded clasts, and within fault breccia matrix. Undifferentiated microfaulting 417.71-419.40m, strongly overprinted by calcite and sericite infilled microfractures, and trace sulphides (py) within the matrix. Fault planes are infilled with palygorskite and overprinted pyrite, with weakly developed slickenlines, and slickensides. >50cm intervals of YBR (same as unit above) within the faulting; Weak overprinting calcite veinlets throughout. Possible sheared sericitic intrafolial slip nearing lower contact. Lower contact is diffuse transitioning into a white brecciated marble.

White brecciated marble. Poorly sorted subangular clasts of strongly bleached marble, suspended within a dark micritic matrix. Trace (1%) disseminated py within matrix, and as fine grained subrounded clasts. Lower contact is gradational and weakens in recrystallized intensity with depth, transitioning into a light grey limestone.

Rock breaks along bedding and exposed bedding planes are rusty brown and strongly lineated. Graphitic near fault (next interval). Grey-greenish to dark grey finegrained exhalite. Several up to 50 cm long patchy to semi-massive euhedral Py intervals with blebby Sph and Gn. Finegrained pervasive disseminated euhedral Py; common Py stringers and veinlets, sometimes include Gn. Intervals are variably moderately to strongly silicified, tends to increase with depth. Common qz stringers / veinlets / veins, often host ankerite (orange to tan, HCL reaction when scratched). Rare Po (at 135.50 m).  Beds host cm thick dark grey chert nodules. Core is variably competent to rubbly with some rare short intervals of fault gouge. Rare vugs. Signs of deformation including rare extensional qz vein arrays, rare boudinaged ankerite veinlet, rare folding. Near end of interval (157 m - 158 m) seafoam green veins (possibly mariposite and/or chlorite?)  in strongly silicified exhalite, associated with Py. Lower contact is gradational with alternating intervals of bleached EXH and silty to sandy 1B.

Dark grey cg sandstone conglomerate, clasts are silicified and variably flattened along bedding. Dark grey fine to medium grained sandstone. Mineralization; pervasive disemminated pyr - occasional pyrite rich beds and occasional blebby euhedral pyr. Sporatic discordant qtz veins with disseminated to blebby pyr with galena and sphalerite occasionally, most noteable that galena and sphalerite are only found in the discordant veins. Thicker qtz veins downhole starting around 228m with pyr, with minor calcite infill towards the mcdame contact. Fracture surfaces are often slickenslides with a chloritic green sheen - soft. Rare deformation features, small scale folding. Around 236m downhole the competency of the core degrades to more rubbly recovery and a fault gouge breccia at 250.6 to 256.1m. Aftre the fault there is a coarsening of the grains to a pebble conglomerate texture, then fining again. At 288.5m a small zone of hydrothermal brecciation with a greenish alteration in the matrix. Competency of the core degrades around 297 to rubbly pieces and a zone of mildly calcareous (UV small patch yellow) medium grained 1B. Approaching the Earn-McDame contact, brecciation increases, carbonate veining increases, mineralization increases.
